intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that spermatogenic failure-103 (SPGF103) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the MEI1 gene (608797) on chromosome 22q13.2.

paragraphs.text: Spermatogenic failure-103 (SPGF103) is an autosomal recessive form of male infertility. Affected men have nonobstructive azoospermia, with spermatogenesis arrested at the spermatocyte stage, or cryptozoospermia. In 1 consanguineous family, a female family member with the same homozygous MEI1 mutation had infertility with embryonic arrest.

checks.claim: Spermatogenic failure-103 (SPGF103) is an autosomal recessive form of male infertility.
checks.evidence_quote: The mutations were inherited from their parents, who were both single heterozygous carriers, indicating a recessive pattern of inheritance.
checks.explanation: Recessive inheritance of a male infertility phenotype; gene is autosomal (22q13.2).

checks.claim: Some men affected with SPGF103 have nonobstructive azoospermia with spermatogenesis arrested at the spermatocyte stage.
checks.evidence_quote: Testicular pathologic analysis and immunohistochemical staining revealed that spermatogenesis is arrested at spermatocyte stage
checks.explanation: The patients had NOA with arrest at the spermatocyte stage.

checks.claim: Some men affected with SPGF103 have cryptozoospermia.

checks.evidence_quote: This study characterized a male infertile patient suffering from azoospermia and a female infertile patient with embryonic arrest from one consanguineous family.
checks.explanation: The title and abstract describe a homozygous deletion found in both patients.

paragraphs.text: Chen et al. (2023) reported 2 infertile Chinese brothers (III:2 and III:3). The proband (III:2) was a 30-year-old man with normal external genitalia and normal serum sex hormone levels. A smear of centrifuged semen sediment showed a sperm count of 0 to 1 cells per high-power field, which indicated cryptozoospermia. In his brother (III:3), several semen tests found no sperm in the initial semen smear. After centrifugation, however, 0 to 1 motile sperm were occasionally seen, which also indicated cryptozoospermia.

paragraphs.text: In 2 Chinese brothers with SPGF103, Chen et al. (2023) identified compound heterozygous mutations in the MEI1 gene. One was a splice site mutation (c.529+5G-A) downstream of exon 5. The other was a c.2071C-G transversion in exon 18, resulting in a gln691-to-glu (Q691E) substitution. Sanger sequencing confirmed the mutations in both brothers. Their father was heterozygous for the c.2071C-G mutation and their mother was heterozygous for the c.529+5G-A mutation. Neither variant was present in the ExAC or gnomAD databases. varSEAK classified the splice variant as class 5, likely to affect splicing, and several prediction programs predicted the missense variant to be deleterious. Functional studies could not be done because too few sperm were available and no testicular tissue was obtained.

paragraphs.text: By whole-exome sequencing, Zhang et al. (2023) identified biallelic MEI1 mutations in 4 Chinese men with nonobstructive azoospermia. The mutations were c.186G-C, c.251delT, and c.1585T-A. In vitro, the c.186G-C missense mutation reduced MEI1 expression and the c.251delT frameshift mutation produced a truncated MEI1 protein. Based on bioinformatic analysis, the authors suggested that the c.1585T-A missense mutation affects the interaction of MEI1 with its partners.

paragraphs.text: In a man with azoospermia and a woman with embryonic arrest from a consanguineous family, Liu et al. (2025) used whole-exome sequencing to identify a homozygous deletion of the whole of exon 19 of the MEI1 gene. Their mother was a heterozygous carrier. cDNA sequencing confirmed the deletion, and exon 19 expression was almost undetectable in the patients. On Western blot of transfected HEK293T cells, the deletion produced a truncated MEI1 protein, consistent with premature termination at exon 20.

paragraphs.text: In a man with azoospermia (SPGF103) and a woman with infertility and embryonic arrest from a consanguineous family, Liu et al. (2025) identified a homozygous deletion of the whole of exon 19 of the MEI1 gene by whole-exome sequencing. Their mother was a heterozygous carrier. cDNA sequencing confirmed the deletion, and exon 19 expression was almost undetectable in the patients. In transfected HEK293T cells, the deletion produced a truncated MEI1 protein, consistent with premature termination at exon 20. Arrested embryos showed high rates of chromosomal anomalies.
